target_customer: US health systems and hospitals (Cleveland Clinic, UTMB, Intermountain named as users)
problem: Health systems have disease risk hidden in routine imaging and heavy manual operational work; Bunkerhill started with opportunistic CT screening and now sells AI agents for hospital workflows.
business_model: Enterprise software sold to health systems (Carebricks agent platform plus FDA cleared clinical algorithms)
product_category: Healthcare AI agents and radiology AI

founders.name: Nishith Khandwala
founders.background_notes: Stanford student with an idea to use AI on existing radiology scans to detect heart disease risk (2017); research assistant at Stanford AIMI Center; Forbes 30 Under 30 healthcare mention on company site.

founders.name: David Eng
founders.background_notes: Listed by Crunchbase as a Stanford course instructor.

technical_complexity.rationale: Opportunistic screening needs trained imaging models and FDA clearance, hard for a student founded team at the time.

defensibility.rationale: FDA clearances and health system integrations are slow to replicate, though radiology AI is crowded and adoption was slow.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established radiology AI vendors focused on triage; opportunistic screening stayed a niche until a CMS reimbursement path was pursued, per Fierce Healthcare.

market_need_then: In 2019 there was no Medicare payment model that supported opportunistic screening, so need was clinical rather than reimbursed, and Fierce Healthcare later noted slow adoption at health systems.

identity.voice_and_tone: Outcome focused (Name the outcome. Bunkerhill delivers.)

branding.brand_signature: Name the outcome tagline and the Carebricks product name
branding.community_and_virality: No evidence found; recognition limited to awards listed by the company.

brand_strength.rationale: Credible among health system buyers but no independent evidence of brand pull.

pivots.to: Agentic AI platform for health systems (Carebricks)
pivots.why: Not stated; Fierce Healthcare notes scaling challenges for screening adoption

outcome_analysis: Bunkerhill came out of Stanford AIMI in YC W19 with FDA cleared imaging algorithms, then moved toward a hospital agent platform. A July 2026 Series B led by Khosla, reported revenue growth of 20x and a dozen plus health systems suggest it has found a buyer base after a slow screening adoption phase.
notes: Series B size conflicts: company press release headlines 55M while Fortune and Fierce report 25M with 55M total raised; 25M used. Series A is poorly documented (Seedtable, Wellfound, VCBacked suggest about 30M in 2023; sources conflict) so not recorded as a round, nor is a Caplight 2019 seed. YC lists founded 2022 while CB Insights says 2019; the YC batch is W19. No 2019 dated competitor sources found, so the list is empty.
